name: Brag Document
summary: A running document where you record your accomplishments, impact, and learning at work, so you don't forget them and can make your case in reviews and promotions.
explanation:
A brag document is a continuously updated list of what you have accomplished, popularized by Julia Evans in her 2019 article 'Get your work recognized: write a brag document'. It is the opposite of relying on memory, your own or your manager's, to know what you did over the last six or twelve months.

## Why It Matters

- **People forget**: You will forget most of what you did by review time. Your manager remembers even less, and may have changed.
- **Invisible work stays invisible**: Mentoring, refactoring, incident handling, documentation, and process improvements rarely show up in metrics unless someone writes them down.
- **It helps with performance reviews and promotions**: You arrive with evidence instead of vague impressions.
- **It counters impostor syndrome**: Reading a concrete list of what you achieved is a reality check against the feeling that you haven't done much.
- **It supports reflection**: Seeing patterns in your work shows you what you are good at and where you want to grow.

## What to Include

- Projects shipped and their impact (numbers when possible)
- Problems solved, especially messy or ambiguous ones
- Collaboration and mentoring
- Design work, documentation, and processes you improved
- Things you learned and skills you developed
- Context and outcomes, not just activities: why it mattered

## How to Keep It

- Update it regularly: weekly or at least monthly, during your weekly review.
- Write it in your own words, honestly. It's for you first.
- Share it with your manager before reviews.
- Keep it in your personal knowledge management system, linked to the relevant projects and notes, so it compounds over the years.

references.title: Get your work recognized: write a brag document - Julia Evans
